claims.text: The 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock produces a bond coat with insufficient thickness.
Changing the feedstock size distribution from 15–45 μm to approximately 45–75 μm will increase coating build-up sufficiently to attain the required thickness.
The 45–75 μm feedstock will preserve coating integrity.
The 45–75 μm feedstock will minimize as-sprayed oxidation.
Larger feedstock particles have a lower surface-area-to-volume ratio than the baseline particles.
The lower surface-area-to-volume ratio of larger particles decreases oxidation before deposition.
Larger particles have improved kinetic energy upon impact.
Larger particles experience less oxidation during spray flight because they reduce the time and area exposed to high-temperature oxidation.
The increased momentum of larger particles promotes better adhesion to the substrate.
The increased momentum of larger particles improves deposition efficiency.
Improved adhesion and deposition efficiency enhance coating build-up without compromising integrity.
Relative to the 15–45 μm baseline, the 45–75 μm feedstock will produce a statistically significant increase in as-sprayed coating thickness.
The larger-particle coating will maintain low oxidation levels and structural integrity while increasing thickness.
The intervention should remain effective under high-temperature and thermal-cycling service typical of thermal barrier coating systems.
Particles exceeding an optimal size range may cause excessive splashing, erosion, nonuniformity, or impaired adhesion.
